finalText:
£800 all-in from the UK is tight for flying anywhere worthwhile in May — but it's a generous budget for one of the world's classic walks on your doorstep: the West Highland Way, 154 km from Milngavie to Fort William, finished off with Ben Nevis if the weather plays.

Budget breakdown for 10 days: trains ~£90 return, campsites and two hostel nights ~£140 (wild camping is legal in Scotland outside the Loch Lomond east-shore restriction zone in summer — carry the map of the camping management zones), food and pub meals ~£250, gear you may need to top up ~£100. Total ~£580, leaving £220 of headroom for a B&B night if the rain gets biblical, which in May it might.

May is the sweet spot: long daylight, few midges yet, and drier than average. Book the Milarrochy Bay campsite ahead for the Saturday night; everything else you can wing.

If you'd rather go abroad, the same budget stretches to the High Tatras in Slovakia (fly to Kraków from ~£60 return, mountain huts ~£25/night) — say the word and I'll plan that instead.
